The singlet at 2.12 ppm suggests a methyl group, likely attached to a carbonyl group, indicating an acetyl group. The aromatic protons are observed between 7.43 and 8.02 ppm, consistent with a substituted benzene ring. The combination of carbon and proton NMR data suggests a structure with an aromatic ring and an acetyl group. To further narrow down the possibilities, I will use the IR spectra to confirm the presence of functional groups, especially carbonyl groups.</thought>
<action>ir_spectra</action>

<thought>The IR spectra show significant peaks at 1791 and 1783 cm⁻¹, which are indicative of carbonyl stretching vibrations, likely from an ester or anhydride. The combination of NMR and IR data suggests a compound with an aromatic ring and carbonyl groups, possibly an aromatic ester or anhydride. Given the data, a likely candidate is an aromatic ester with an acetyl group. I will now search for a SMILES string that matches these characteristics using the NMRShift database.</thought>

The aromatic carbon shifts and the presence of a carbonyl group are also consistent with the observed spectra.
